chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Guitar heritage: Eddie Durham, trombonists playing guitar, Christian's sources
summary: The first black guitarist who influenced him was Eddie Durham, a trombonist, and he urges young guitarists to ask who influenced Christian.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: But, as I said, this is to show you how these things go right down the line. So that is where it all began, you know, and I think that they should kind of check back, you know, and -- see, now, as I told you, the first black guitarist that I heard, that really should I say influenced me was Eddie Durham. And he was a trombonist, but a marvelous guitarist, and there was another one and I can't think -- here's another trombonist. His name was Coffee and he played very fine guitar. I'm trying to think whose band he was with, and I can't remember. His last name was Coffee. It seemed as if all the trombone players were playing guitar then.

But as I say, this -- the kids should really look back and see, you know, go back and listen to what was happening. And on guitar a lot of them are, because a lot of them are listening to Christian, you know. But it didn't -- who was Christian influenced by. See, this is -- someone told me and Led Belly I forgot. Oh, it wasn't Led Belly. I forget who it was, it'll come to me in a moment. But these are the things that I would advise them to do.
